findings.text:
[Medium / P1] Await refusal persistence before releasing the import lock.

Returning this promise without `await` enters `finally` immediately. For a folder import, `created` is empty, so `#current` is cleared while `#recordRefusedConversion` is still awaiting `mkdir`/write/rename. A second import of the same HTML can enter; both use the same `<sha256>.html.partial`, and competing renames can make one attempt return `failed` without its rejected-import row. This violates `docs/development.md:112` (one diagnostic attempt row per rejection). A diagnostic extracting both production methods, with preparation/filesystem operations mocked in memory, admitted two concurrent refusals and reproduced the second rename failing with ENOENT and only one attempt row. Use `return await` (or otherwise retain ownership until persistence settles), and add a regression that delays refusal persistence and requires a second import to receive the busy response until it finishes.

tests.name: answers a second import of the same HTML with the busy message until the first has written its attempt row

findings.text:
[Medium / P1] Require a successful parity outcome, not only eligible evidence.

The parity scorecard writes `result` and `exit`, not `ok` (`scripts/parity/run.mjs:229–232`). Thus a current-head `{evidence:true,result:'FAIL',exit:1,freshBuild:{head}}` passes all these predicates and gives `gate-v5` PASS; a missing outcome passes too. `evidence:true` describes run eligibility, not success, and this runner does not execute/check the preceding gate's exit itself. Require the suite-specific success fields, full 42-view coverage and strict-register mode, and reject absent outcomes. Add negative scorecard fixtures for failed, incomplete and missing outcomes. This is unchanged from PR #74 and contradicts GRS-24 acceptance item 1.

findings.text:
[Medium / P1] Make source-to-original discrepancies affect the contract verdict.

`pathOther`, `sizeDiffers` and `realPathDiffers` only enter the output tally; only `unavailable` fails. If a converter deterministically maps a row to another valid original, reconversion and byte verification still agree with that wrong mapping, and this step can report PASS. A focused run of this block with source `expected.txt`/10 bytes and a verified indexed `wrong.txt`/20 bytes reports both mismatches with no problems. Require independent source locator/size agreement, with any legitimate normalization or declared-size exception explicitly accounted for, and add wrong-but-existing-original and size-mismatch negative cases. This carries forward the PR #74 finding against GRS-24 item 3's correct-original-mappings requirement; it does not claim the current private sample is mis-mapped.

findings.text:
[Low / P2] Keep coverage notes beyond the first 100 accessible.

A valid conversion report can contain more than 100 notes for one code. `sourceCoverage` returns `total:101` but only 100 items, and its Svelte section provides no pagination or way to inspect the omitted subjects/messages. That contradicts the CC-25 F1 fix's promise to show every converter coverage note and leaves later unsupported data without its repair detail. Render every note or provide bounded paging/expansion with explicit truncation information; cover 101 notes in the regression. This is the unchanged low follow-up from PR #74; the documented sample counts remain below this limit.
